title: SSC MTS 2026
meta_description: SSC MTS 2026 - Multi Tasking Staff exam for 10th pass candidates. Sep-Nov 2026 exam dates, salary ₹18-22K/month, Physical Efficiency Test, Group C posts.

hero.one_liner: Government jobs for 10th pass - Multi Tasking Staff (Group C) posts in central government ministries, offices, and departments across India

what_is_it: SSC MTS (Multi Tasking Staff) is one of the easiest government exams to crack, requiring only 10th class pass qualification. It recruits for Group C non-gazetted, non-ministerial posts in various central government ministries, departments, and offices. MTS staff handle tasks like physical maintenance of records, general cleanliness, carrying files, photocopying, and other support functions in government offices.

The exam is conducted annually by SSC with typically 8,000-10,000 vacancies. The selection process has a single Computer Based Test (CBT) followed by a Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Document Verification. The exam is bilingual (English + Hindi) and relatively straightforward - testing basic General Intelligence, Numerical Aptitude, General English, and General Awareness at the 10th class level.

Starting salary is at Pay Level 1 (₹18,000-56,900 basic pay scale). With Dearness Allowance and other allowances, the in-hand salary is approximately ₹18,000-22,000 per month. While this is the lowest pay scale in central government, MTS employees get all government benefits - job security, medical insurance, LTC, children's education allowance, pension (under NPS), and paid leaves.

For 2026, per the SSC Calendar 2026-27, the notification is expected on 30 June 2026 with the exam scheduled for September-November 2026. This makes it one of the later SSC exams in the calendar year.

extra_sections.heading: What Does an MTS Employee Actually Do?
content: The 'Multi Tasking' in MTS means you perform various support tasks in a government office. Daily work typically includes:
Physical record management - carrying files between sections, arranging and maintaining old records in record rooms, binding and labeling files.
Office maintenance - general cleanliness of the office section, arranging furniture, managing stationery supplies, operating photocopier/printer.
Support duties - serving water/tea during meetings, carrying messages between officers, managing the dispatch section, answering basic phone calls.

Some MTS posts in specific departments have different duties: CBIC Havaldar involves manning entry gates, checking passes, and security-related tasks. MTS in post offices may involve mail sorting and delivery assistance.
Important reality check: MTS is the lowest rung in central government hierarchy. The work is manual/physical in nature.

However, it comes with permanent government job security, all benefits, and the opportunity to appear for departmental exams (like LDC exam) to get promoted to higher clerical posts. Many MTS employees have moved to LDC and UDC positions within 3-5 years through departmental promotions.

extra_sections.heading: Physical Efficiency Test (PET) - Requirements
content: After clearing the CBT, candidates must pass a Physical Efficiency Test. This is qualifying - not merit-based.
You just need to complete the tasks within the given time:
Males: Walk 1.6 km in 15 minutes, Cycle 8 km in 25 minutes.
Females: Walk 1 km in 20 minutes, Cycle 3 km in 25 minutes.
PwBD candidates are exempted from PET.
These are very basic physical fitness requirements - not athletic standards. Most young, reasonably fit candidates clear this easily.
Practice by walking/cycling regularly in the weeks before PET. Wear comfortable shoes and sports clothing on PET day.
Proper sleep and nutrition in the week before PET matter more than last-minute training.

extra_sections.heading: Why SSC MTS is ideal for 10th pass candidates
content: SSC MTS is the simplest government exam - one computer-based test with basic questions from school-level syllabus. No interview, no physical test, no typing test.
Just clear the CBT and you're in. The exam is designed for Group C (Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial) posts like peon, watchman, gardener, and cleaning staff in central government offices.
Don't let the job title discourage you. MTS posts carry Pay Level 1 (Rs 18,000 basic) with total monthly salary of Rs 28,000-35,000 including DA, HRA, and transport allowance.
Plus all government benefits - medical, pension, LTC, and job security until age 60. After 5 years, you can appear for departmental exams for promotion to LDC/UDC.

extra_sections.heading: Preparation in 3 months
content: Month 1: Focus on Numerical Ability - BODMAS, percentage, ratio, average, time-speed-distance at Class 8-10 level. Practice 30 questions daily from RS Aggarwal or Kiran's SSC Mathematics.
This is the most scoring section for those who practice.
Month 2: Reasoning - coding-decoding, analogy, series, blood relations, direction sense. These are pattern-based questions that improve dramatically with practice.
Solve one chapter per day from any reasoning book. General Awareness - start reading a current affairs magazine and revise basic GK (history, geography, polity).
Month 3: Solve previous year papers and mock tests. SSC repeats question patterns - if you've solved 10 years of papers, you'll recognize 40-50% of questions in the actual exam.
English section tests basic grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension - daily newspaper reading for 30 minutes is sufficient preparation.

extra_sections.heading: MTS to LDC promotion - the career path
extra_sections.content:
MTS employees can take departmental exams (LDCE) after 5 years of service to get promoted to LDC (Pay Level 2). LDC can further promote to UDC (Pay Level 4) and then to Assistant (Pay Level 6).

The career progression is slow but guaranteed - you retire at a decent level with full pension benefits.

extra_sections.heading: CBT exam pattern - what to expect
content: SSC MTS CBT has 4 sections: Numerical and Mathematical Ability (20 questions, 20 marks), Reasoning Ability and Problem Solving (20 questions, 20 marks), English Language and Comprehension (25 questions, 25 marks), and General Awareness (25 questions, 25 marks). Total 90 questions, 90 marks, in 90 minutes.
Negative marking: 1 mark deducted per wrong answer.
The difficulty level is genuinely easy - all questions are at Class 8-10 level. If you've completed 10th standard, you already know most of the content.
The challenge is not difficulty but competition - with 40-50 lakh applicants for 8,000 vacancies, even small mistakes eliminate candidates. Accuracy is everything.
Session-wise normalization: SSC conducts MTS in multiple shifts across several days. To ensure fairness, scores are normalized across sessions using a statistical formula.

This means a harder session's raw score gets boosted while an easier session's score gets slightly reduced. You can't control which session you get - just focus on maximizing your relative performance.

extra_sections.heading: Subject-wise detailed strategy
content: Numerical Ability (20 questions): Topics - Number System (HCF, LCM, factors, divisibility rules), Percentage (direct calculation and application in profit-loss, discount), Ratio and Proportion, Average, Time-Speed-Distance (train problems, boats and streams), Time and Work, Simple and Compound Interest, basic Geometry (area and perimeter of rectangle, triangle, circle), and basic Algebra.
Every single question is from Class 8-10 NCERT mathematics. Don't waste time on advanced topics like trigonometry, coordinate geometry, or complex algebra - they're not tested in MTS.
Solve RS Aggarwal's arithmetic chapters on the topics listed above. Practice 25 questions daily.
Master the basics and you'll score 16+ out of 20.

Reasoning Ability (20 questions): Analogy (word and number pairs), Classification (odd one out from a group), Series completion (number series, letter series, mixed series), Coding-Decoding (letter shifting, number coding), Blood Relations (family tree problems), Direction and Distance, Mirror Image and Water Image, Venn Diagrams, and Calendar problems.

Reasoning is the most scoring section because it's entirely practice-dependent - there's nothing to memorize, just patterns to recognize. Solve 30 reasoning questions daily from any SSC reasoning book.
Start with easy chapters (analogy, classification) and progress to harder ones (blood relations, calendar). Within 6 weeks, you'll consistently score 17+ out of 20.

English Language (25 questions): Reading Comprehension (1 passage, 5-7 questions), Sentence Correction/Error Spotting, Fill in the blanks (vocabulary and grammar), Synonym and Antonym, Idioms and Phrases, One Word Substitution, Spelling Correction. The difficulty is moderate - harder than MTS math but easier than CGL English.

For English improvement, read simple English daily - newspaper headlines, short articles, or even English subtitles while watching shows. Don't try to memorize word lists - contextual learning is more effective.
Practice 2 comprehension passages daily. For grammar, learn 5 common error types: subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, preposition usage, article usage, and pronoun reference.
These cover 80% of error spotting questions.

General Awareness (25 questions): Indian History (ancient civilizations, medieval rulers, freedom movement, post-independence India), Indian Geography (physical features, rivers, climate, natural resources, states and capitals), Indian Polity (fundamental rights, Parliament, President, judiciary, local governance), General Science (physics concepts, chemical reactions, biology basics), Current Affairs (last 6 months - government schemes, awards, sports, international events).
GK preparation tip: Don't try to cover everything - focus on high-frequency topics. Analyze previous year MTS papers (2019-2024) and identify the 50 topics that appear most frequently.
These 50 topics cover approximately 60% of the GK section. History focuses on freedom movement, Geography on Indian rivers and climate, Polity on fundamental rights and constitutional amendments.

extra_sections.heading: Study plan - 10th pass to MTS selection in 4 months
content: Month 1 - Build basics: Math - complete arithmetic from RS Aggarwal (one chapter per day). Reasoning - complete analogy, classification, series, coding-decoding from any reasoning book.
English - start reading one newspaper editorial daily (use Google Translate for difficult words). GK - start reading Lucent's General Knowledge (50 pages per week).
Month 2 - Practice phase: Math - solve 50 previous year MTS math questions daily. Reasoning - complete blood relations, direction, calendar, Venn diagrams.
Move to solving 50 previous year reasoning questions daily. English - start error spotting and fill-in-the-blanks practice.
GK - complete Lucent's GK + start monthly current affairs compilation.
Month 3 - Mock test phase: Take 1 full-length mock test daily. After each mock, spend 30 minutes analyzing wrong answers.
Track your accuracy per section - identify which topics you consistently get wrong and revise them. Continue daily newspaper reading for current affairs.
Revise Lucent's GK every weekend.
Month 4 - Final revision: Take 2 mock tests daily (morning and evening). Focus entirely on accuracy - attempt 70-75 questions confidently instead of rushing through all 90.
Revise your error log from all previous mocks. Revise current affairs of the last 3 months intensively.
Stop studying new topics 3 days before the exam - only revise what you know.

extra_sections.heading: Life after selection - MTS employee benefits
content: MTS employees are posted in central government offices - ministries in Delhi, regional offices across India, field offices, and attached offices. The work involves office support tasks: file management, photocopying, delivering files between departments, maintaining office records, assisting higher-level staff, and basic computer operations.
The daily routine is fixed: 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday to Friday. No overtime, no weekend work, no night shifts.
This predictability is invaluable for family life - something private sector jobs at this salary level rarely offer. You know exactly when you'll be home every day, every week, every year.
Benefits breakdown: Basic pay Rs 18,000 + DA (50%+) = Rs 27,000. HRA (8-24% of basic depending on city) = Rs 1,440-4,320.
Transport allowance = Rs 1,350-3,600. Total monthly salary: Rs 30,000-35,000 in tier 2 cities, Rs 33,000-40,000 in Delhi/metros.
Additionally: CGHS medical coverage (free treatment for entire family), LTC (travel twice yearly), children education allowance, and NPS pension contribution.

Promotion path: MTS (Pay Level 1) → after departmental exam, promoted to LDC (Pay Level 2, Rs 19,900 basic) → UDC (Pay Level 4, Rs 25,500) → Head Clerk/Superintendent. The LDCE (Limited Departmental Competitive Exam) for promotion from MTS to LDC is conducted periodically - prepare for it from your first year of joining.
Promotees from MTS often reach Assistant level (Pay Level 6, Rs 35,400) by retirement.

extra_sections.heading: Previous year cutoff analysis
content: SSC MTS cutoffs vary by state and category. General category cutoffs for recent cycles: Delhi/NCR - 108-115 out of 270 (normalized), Maharashtra - 100-108, UP - 95-105, Bihar - 90-100, West Bengal - 85-95, South Indian states - 80-90.
These are approximate ranges and vary each cycle based on vacancies and applicant quality.

The low cutoff numbers (relative to total marks) are misleading - normalization adjusts raw scores significantly. A raw score of 55 out of 90 in an easy session might become a normalized score of 95, while the same raw score in a hard session might become 115.
Focus on maximizing your raw score relative to the difficulty of your specific session.
Category-wise cutoff difference: OBC cutoff is typically 5-8 points below general. SC cutoff is 15-20 points below general.
ST cutoff is 20-25 points below general. EWS cutoff is close to general (2-5 points lower).
These gaps mean reserved category candidates have a tangible advantage - ensure your category certificate is valid and submitted correctly.
Year-over-year trend: Cutoffs have been increasing as more candidates prepare seriously using free online resources and coaching apps. What scored a selection 5 years ago might not be enough today.
Target a raw score of 65+ out of 90 to be safe across most states and categories.

extra_sections.heading: Best books and free resources
content: Mathematics: Kiran's SSC Mathematics (previous year chapterwise) is the single best book for MTS math preparation. It contains 5,000+ previous year questions organized by topic with solutions.
Complete this one book and your math preparation is done. Alternative: RS Aggarwal Arithmetic for concept building if your basics are weak.
Reasoning: Kiran's SSC Reasoning or RS Aggarwal Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning. Both cover all MTS reasoning topics comprehensively.
Complete any ONE book - don't buy multiple reasoning books. Supplement with daily reasoning quizzes on Testbook or Adda247 apps (free daily tests available).

English: Objective General English by SP Bakshi covers grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension at the right level for MTS. For daily reading practice, use Grammarly's blog posts or BBC Learning English - both are free and at intermediate level.
Don't read advanced English literature - MTS tests basic comprehension, not literary analysis.
General Knowledge: Lucent's General Knowledge is the bible for SSC GK. It covers history, geography, polity, science, and economy in one book.
Read it cover to cover twice - first for understanding, second for memorization. Supplement with a monthly current affairs magazine (Pratiyogita Darpan, Jagran Josh, or any SSC-focused compilation).

Free online resources: SSC's official website (ssc.nic.in) has previous year papers with answer keys - download all MTS papers from 2017 onwards. YouTube channels like Rakesh Yadav Readers (math), Abhinay Sharma (reasoning), and Adda247 English offer free complete courses specifically for SSC MTS level.
The Testbook app offers 200+ free MTS mock tests.

extra_sections.heading: Application process - step by step
content: Step 1: SSC One-Time Registration at ssc.nic.in. Create an account with your email and mobile number.

Fill personal details, educational qualification, and upload photo (passport size, 20-50 KB JPEG) and signature (10-20 KB JPEG). This registration is valid for all SSC exams - you do it once and use for MTS, CHSL, CGL, etc.
Step 2: When MTS notification is released, log into your SSC account and click 'Apply' for MTS exam. Select your preferred exam center region (choose 3 cities in order of preference).
Fill any additional details specific to MTS notification. Verify all information carefully - corrections after submission are limited.
Step 3: Pay the application fee - Rs 100 for general and OBC male candidates. Female candidates, SC, ST, PwD, and ESM (Ex-Servicemen) are exempted from the fee.
Payment via debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI. Save the payment receipt and application printout.
Step 4: Download admit card 2-3 weeks before the exam from ssc.nic.in. The admit card contains your exam date, shift, center address, and roll number.
Carry a color printout of the admit card along with original photo ID (Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, or passport) to the exam center. No electronic devices allowed inside the center.

extra_sections.heading: Post-selection training and posting
content: After selection, you'll receive an appointment letter from the allotted ministry or department. There's no formal training academy for MTS - you join directly at your posting location and learn on the job.
Senior staff members guide you through office procedures, file management, and departmental workflows during the first few weeks.

Posting locations depend on the vacancies you were selected against. If selected under a specific ministry (like Ministry of Finance or Ministry of Home Affairs), your posting will be in that ministry's offices.
Delhi has the maximum MTS postings since most central government ministries are headquartered there. Regional postings are in attached offices, subordinate offices, and field offices across India.
Transfer policy: MTS employees can request transfers after completing 2-3 years at a posting. Transfers within the same ministry are easier than inter-ministry transfers.

Mutual transfer (swapping postings with another MTS employee in a different city) is a common and faster method. Compassionate ground transfers (family medical emergency, spouse posting) get priority consideration.

Work environment: Government offices provide a structured, low-stress work environment compared to private sector jobs at similar salary levels. Fixed working hours (9:30-6:00), no performance targets, no risk of layoff, and respectful treatment from colleagues.

The pace of work is relaxed - you won't face the high-pressure deadlines common in private companies. For many 10th pass candidates from small towns, an MTS posting in a central government ministry represents life-changing upward mobility.

extra_sections.text: SSC MTS is proof that you do not need a degree to get a central government job - Class 10 pass candidates can secure a permanent posting in ministries and government offices across India.

preparation_tips: The entire exam is at 10th class difficulty level. Revise your Class 9-10 Math (percentage, ratio, average, profit-loss, geometry basics), Science (physics, chemistry, biology basics), and Social Studies (history, geography, civics).

For General English, focus on basic grammar - tenses, articles, prepositions, one-word substitutions, synonyms/antonyms, and sentence correction. Read 10th class English textbook if your English is weak. NCERT Class 10 English is perfect preparation.
Previous year papers are the BEST resource for SSC MTS. The patterns repeat heavily. Solve 20+ previous year papers and you'll see 40-50% similar questions in the actual exam.

General Awareness covers static GK (capitals, currencies, important days, first in India, Indian history basics) + last 6 months current affairs. One monthly current affairs magazine is sufficient. Follow The Hindu for daily news.

Time management is easier in MTS than CGL/CHSL - you have 54 seconds per question (vs 36 seconds in CGL). Use this advantage. Don't rush - focus on accuracy since the negative marking penalty (25%) is significant.
Practice physical efficiency: start walking/cycling 2-3 weeks before PET. The distances are short - even unfit candidates can clear with basic training.

faqs.question: Is MTS a permanent government job?
faqs.answer:
Yes. SSC MTS is a permanent, pensionable central government job.

You get all benefits - job security, medical insurance, LTC, children's education allowance, pension (under NPS), and paid leaves. It's not contractual or temporary.

faqs.question: Can I get promoted from MTS?
faqs.answer:
Yes. MTS employees can appear for departmental exams (like the LDC limited departmental exam) to get promoted to Lower Division Clerk (Level 2).

From LDC, promotions to UDC, Assistant, and higher posts are possible. Promotion from MTS to LDC typically takes 3-5 years of service eligibility.

faqs.question: MTS salary seems low. Is it worth it?
faqs.answer: ₹18,000-22,000/month may seem low, but consider: (1) It's a permanent govt job with zero risk of layoff, (2) Medical insurance for entire family, (3) Pension after retirement (NPS), (4) Annual increments + DA revisions increase salary over time, (5) Promotion opportunities exist, (6) In many tier-3 cities, ₹20K is a decent salary. For someone with only 10th pass qualification, MTS is one of the best career options available.

faqs.question: I have a graduation degree. Should I apply for MTS?
faqs.answer:
You CAN apply (over-qualification is allowed), but you SHOULD focus on CGL (for graduates) and CHSL (for 12th pass) which offer much higher posts and salaries. Use MTS only as a backup safety net.

Many graduates apply for MTS as insurance while primarily targeting CGL/CHSL.

faqs.question: Is there typing test in MTS?
faqs.answer:
No. There is no typing test, skill test, or computer proficiency test in SSC MTS.

The selection is based purely on CBT score + PET (qualifying). This makes MTS accessible to candidates who may not have typing or computer skills.

faqs.question: What happens after getting selected as MTS?
faqs.answer:
After selection, you go through Document Verification (verify your original documents), Medical Examination (health check), and Training. The training period is typically 2-4 weeks at a training center where you learn office procedures and rules.

After training, you're posted to a central government office in your preferred region (subject to vacancy and suitability).

faqs.question: Is SSC MTS a good career option?
faqs.answer:
For 10th pass candidates, absolutely. No other option offers Rs 28,000-35,000/month salary with lifetime job security, pension, medical, and free housing/HRA for 10th pass qualification.

While the starting role is basic (peon/watchman), promotions to LDC/UDC are available through departmental exams after 5 years.

faqs.question: What is the SSC MTS age limit?
faqs.answer:
18-25 years for general category. SC/ST: 18-30, OBC: 18-28, PwD: 18-35.

Ex-servicemen get 3 years relaxation beyond the specific category limit. No limit on number of attempts within the age bracket.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in SSC MTS?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Each correct answer carries 3 marks and each wrong answer deducts 1 mark.

With 100 questions in 90 minutes, focus on accuracy over speed. Attempt 60-70 questions with high confidence rather than rushing through all 100 with guesses.

faqs.question: Can I apply for both SSC MTS and SSC CHSL?
faqs.answer:
Yes. MTS requires 10th pass, CHSL requires 12th pass.

If you've completed 12th, apply for both - the syllabus overlaps 80%. CHSL gives you a higher-paying post (LDC/DEO vs MTS).

Use MTS as backup while aiming for CHSL. Many candidates clear both and choose CHSL for better pay and work profile.

study_plan.tasks: SSC MTS is 10th-level. Focus on basic maths - percentage, ratio, average, time & work. Start Lucent GK. English vocabulary 15 words/day. Reasoning basics from R.S. Aggarwal.
Solve last 5 years SSC MTS papers. One mock test per week. Focus on speed - 25 questions in 45 minutes per section. Current affairs of last 6 months.
Daily mock tests. Revise GK notes. Focus on accuracy - negative marking is 0.25. Target: 80+ out of 100 for safe selection.
